source.title: Dissecting Supervised Constrastive Learning
source.authors: Florian Graf; Christoph Hofer; M. Niethammer; Roland Kwitt

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests fitting as label corruption rises and reports that supervised contrastive training scales superlinearly and fails to reach zero error beyond a corruption threshold under its iteration budget. It compares this with cross-entropy and a fixed-classifier variant.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for prior cross-entropy results; those cited results are not rows. Figure 8 reports time-to-fit curves, with values shown only graphically. The text describes the trends and states that SC cannot achieve zero error beyond 80% corruption on CIFAR10.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training-set fitting and convergence as label corruption increases. CE and CE-fix show approximately linear time-to-fit growth; SC shows superlinear growth and explicitly fails to reach zero training error above 80% corruption on CIFAR10 within the training budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label conclusion: CE and CE-fix scale approximately linearly with corruption, whereas SC scales superlinearly and cannot reach zero error above 80% corruption on CIFAR10 within the tested budget. Batch interactions are the authors' proposed explanation, not an isolated causal finding. The paper's broader conclusion is that the losses have similar minimizing representation geometries but different optimization dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a ResNet-18 on CIFAR10/100 with stochastic gradient descent, but compares CE and supervised contrastive training under the paper's own setup and finite iteration budget.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss function (CE, CE-fix, SC), dataset (CIFAR10 versus CIFAR100), and label-corruption fraction change time-to-fit; SC's CIFAR10 fit failure is stated beyond 80% corruption.
record.problems: Random-label results are presented as figure-only values with no uncertainty estimates. Training is capped at 100k iterations, and the paper reports no test error for the corruption experiments. For SC, the CIFAR10 zero-error failure is stated beyond 80% corruption.
record.rows_left_out: none; all six plotted corruption conditions for each of CE, CE-fix and SC on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 are included. Values are figure only because Figure 8 provides curves without tabulated numbers.

untested.parts: Chance test error; residual error in the SC failure condition; whether near-zero fitting remains possible there. Identical architecture and hyperparameters across corruption levels are not explicitly documented beyond the common setup; matching the original papers' hyperparameters is not required by V1.
A numerical small constant-factor comparison between fully random and true labels, and wall-clock training cost. Reported time-to-fit measures iterations.
All shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel and Gaussian-noise input conditions.
Test error across corruption levels, steady degradation toward chance, and direct evidence of preserving remaining signal while memorizing noise.

Dropout; confirmed augmentation conditions for the random-label experiments; removal of regularization and resulting true-label generalization. Figure 7 varies augmentation but retains L2 regularization.
Within-training ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels; comparisons of total convergence times do not measure that ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied figure transcription exposes axes but not curve coordinates, so exact iteration values and the asserted six-point sampling grid cannot be independently verified. Point-level SC states should not be inferred from aggregate scaling. The paper names CIFAR10 for the failure threshold, although its following 500-versus-5,000 explanation compares class sizes across datasets; retain the explicit dataset attribution and flag that explanatory ambiguity. The 500k-iteration supplement concerns clean-label geometry and does not extend the random-label convergence budget.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance is not reported; the paper does not establish that architecture and training hyperparameters were unchanged from the original sources.
The paper reports relative scaling with corruption, not a numeric constant-factor comparison of time to fit true versus random labels.
Test error rising toward chance and capture of remaining signal are not measured. SC does not fit perfectly at all corruption levels under the stated iteration budget.
